newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZCC clears CentralPower to buy Electro Power.
newsitem.headline: NZCC clears CentralPower to buy Electro Power.

text.p: The New Zealand Commerce Commission said on Friday it had cleared CentralPower to acquire 100 percent of Electro Power.
The commission said a merger of the two unlisted North Island companies would result in limited aggregation in the competitive national retail electricity market.
It would also result in a minimal loss of cross-border competition in the merged entity's electricity distribution market.
"However, that loss of competition is not such that it would give rise to dominance concerns," the commission said.

CentralPower and Electro Power announced their plan to merge on October 18, saying it would create New Zealand's 10th largest electricity distribution company, with total assets of NZ$130 million and annual energy sales of $75 million.
Infrastructure and Utilities NZ Ltd (Infratil) owns 21 percent of CentralPower, which is based in the Manawatu region of the North Island.
